title: SYNC Information and Entertainment Component Locations
introduction:
The dashboard is only the visible end of the entertainment system. I read this drawing like a venue plan: the controls and display are on stage, while modules, microphones and antenna cables do much of their work out of sight. This reference applies to the SYNC configuration named in the section heading.

Find the component description in the table, then follow its inset picture’s leader to the endpoint on the vehicle. The insets show component shapes; the endpoints show their installed locations. The drawing combines coupe and convertible equipment, so select the description that matches the body style before treating a rear speaker, antenna or microphone location as applicable. A front antenna cable is explicitly marked as not shown.

The APIM—Accessory Protocol Interface Module—handles connected-device, voice and media functions and is behind the FCDIM, the front control/display interface module. The GPSM is the global positioning system module. The ACM is the audio front control module; DACMC means digital audio control module C, whose engine applicability remains identified in the table. These names help distinguish the boxes behind the dashboard rather than treating the screen as the whole system.

Read the directional abbreviations as vehicle locations: LHF and RHF mean left-hand front and right-hand front; LHR and RHR mean left-hand rear and right-hand rear. The table also distinguishes the front and rear USB paths and the body-specific antenna arrangements. Use this map to identify the relevant component and configuration, then consult matching service or diagnostic information for access or testing. Cable routes here do not establish connector pinouts or electrical test points.

edits.text: ANC (active noise control) microphones apply to 2.3L only. On a coupe, they are in the overhead console and at the center rear of the headliner. On a convertible, they are in the overhead console, the RHR quarter panel and the LHR quarter panel.
edits.why: The separately listed SYNC® microphone serves the voice-input side of the system. I check the engine and body-style qualifiers before using an ANC microphone location, because this combined drawing shows equipment alternatives.
